answer: Sybil resistance rests on a stake-priced identity gate. Each agent locks a refundable bond scaled to the influence it claims, slashed if two identities share a controller. A newcomer enters the reward set only through an inlet of independent attestations: a bonded party co-signs and posts a deposit that burns on collusion. A wharf of throwaway keys cannot pass, since every fake agent costs a real bond plus a real attestation. Reputation, like nectar, accrues only to a staked identity and dies if cloned. Attack cost rises with clones while payout per agent stays flat, so farming loses money.
